what_its_for: Dantrolene is used to treat muscle spasticity (stiffness and tightness) caused by conditions such as stroke, cerebral palsy, spinal cord injury, or multiple sclerosis. It is also used to treat and prevent a rare but life-threatening reaction to anesthesia called malignant hyperthermia, where muscles suddenly become very rigid and body temperature spikes dangerously high.
how_to_take: Take dantrolene capsules by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. If the capsule is hard to swallow, you may carefully open it and mix the powder into fruit juice or another liquid and drink it right away. Do not crush or chew the capsule contents if possible.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the dose that works best for you with the fewest side effects. For muscle spasticity in adults, the usual starting dose is 25 mg once daily, which may be increased up to 100 mg taken 2 to 4 times per day as needed. The maximum dose is 400 mg per day. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is determined by the doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store dantrolene capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking dantrolene, as it can increase dizziness, drowsiness, and the risk of liver problems. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause significant drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as dantrolene may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxants, opioid pain relievers, and certain blood pressure medications, as they can interact with dantrolene.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark urine, severe nausea or vomiting, stomach pain, or unusual tiredness — these may be signs of serious liver problems. Also call your doctor if you experience severe muscle weakness that makes it hard to breathe or swallow, chest pain, difficulty breathing, blood in your urine, or severe skin rash. Call your doctor if your muscle spasms are not improving after 45 days of treatment, or if your side effects are bothering you.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in muscle stiffness within a few days to a couple of weeks of starting treatment. However, it often takes 4 to 6 weeks of gradually increasing doses to see the full benefit. Your doctor may stop the medication if you do not show meaningful improvement after 45 days at the highest tolerated dose. Be patient and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Liver disease: Dantrolene can cause serious liver damage and should NOT be used in patients with active liver disease such as hepatitis or cirrhosis. Your doctor will monitor your liver function with blood tests regularly. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and weakness, increasing the risk of falls — use extra caution. Pregnancy: This medication should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, as it may harm the unborn baby; discuss risks and benefits with your doctor. Breastfeeding: Dantrolene passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is generally not recommended while taking this medication. Children: Dantrolene can be used in children over 5 years old for spasticity, with doses carefully adjusted by weight by the doctor.
